line_or_section: notes item 2; analyse.py main() and board_predictions()
finding: Fix for B01/B02 does not hold for the six pqm4 clean rows (BP19 to BP21, BP25 to BP27). The notes count them as out of sample and inside the refutation rule, but their registered 95 percent intervals are built from the test half errors (test_err), which include the residuals of these same six published rows. Their published values are already inside the intervals, so a board that reproduces pqm4 scores six automatic hits. With 24 rows and a one third rule, the 18 harness rows (the only genuine model test) could miss 8 of 18 (44 percent) and the model would still not be refuted.
evidence: analyse.py main(): test_err = rows.loc[rows['half']=='test','err_pct_fitted'] is passed to board_predictions and prediction_interval for every BP row; split.csv puts S2-0019..21 and S2-0028..30 in the test half; recomputed: published cycles of all 12 pqm4 B0 rows lie inside pi95_lo/hi_modelled.
suggested_fix: State in a further dated note that BP19 to BP21 and BP25 to BP27 are not blind (their own residuals set the interval width and their values were known) and report them with BP22 to BP30 as a board check; apply the registered rule to the 18 harness rows only, and report the miss share there.

finding: Statistic mismatch: the point predictions and intervals for sign are means (model trained on pqm4 averages; harness value is the mean over traced messages), but each prediction is scored by whether the board measured median lies inside the interval. Signing time is right skewed by rejection sampling, so the median sits below the mean; sign rows (BP2, BP5, BP8, BP20, BP23) are biased toward a low miss. Board runs use ITERS=100 messages while the harness trace used 11, so the message mix also differs.
evidence: board_predictions.csv: model 'fitted NNLS', instructions_sd_emulated for ML-DSA-44 harness sign 1.54e6 on a mean of 4.25e6; RTL_SIM_RESULTS shows ML-DSA-44 sign min 7.57e6, median 12.55e6, max 36.3e6; bench/mcu/Makefile ITERS ?= 100.
suggested_fix: Add a dated note that sign rows will be scored on the board mean (and median reported beside it), or that sign rows are scored separately; record the message count and seed used on the board.

finding: Fix for B04 only records cache state; it does not say what happens to the verdict. The protocol's own benchmark clock modes have caches on for both candidate boards (L4R5ZI: data and instruction cache and prefetch; F4 Discovery: data and instruction cache), so every one of the 30 rows will be measured under conditions the hashed file says the model excludes ('no cache'). The pqm4 training rows were themselves produced in that cached mode, so the 'no cache' condition is also inconsistent with the training data.
evidence: BOARD_RUN_PROTOCOL.md lines 41 to 44; notes item 3 says rows 'will be marked as such beside its verdict' with no rule on counting them; PREDICTIONS_V4_BOARD.md line 5 'no cache'.
suggested_fix: State in a dated note whether rows measured with caches on count toward the refutation rule, and state that at zero wait states the cache effect is expected to be small (with a source) or plan a cache off pass.

finding: The 'Multiple of baseline' and rate comparisons mix native and proxy rows on the same target. On ESP32-C3 the Ed25519 baseline is native RISC-V (2,952,000) while ML-DSA-87, XMSS, SLH-DSA and ML-KEM are Cortex-M4 proxies, giving multiples such as ML-DSA-87 1.42 against ML-DSA-44 1.25 (native) and XMSS 4.43 against 18.1 on the M4: the ratios reflect the core mix, not the schemes. On TurtleBot3 ML-DSA-44 is a native SLOTHY Cortex-M7 DTCM row (813,339) compared with an M4 proxy Ed25519 row, which favours ML-DSA.
evidence: Table rows in section 2 and 3; S7-009 is Cortex-M7 at 24 MHz from DTCM (2025/366 Section 5 'We only use the DTCM memory'); recomputed 4,193,104/2,952,000 = 1.42.
suggested_fix: Leave the multiple blank when numerator and baseline come from different cores, or compute it only from the same core rows, and say so in the table note.

finding: The Ed25519 source (Owens et al., Table II) also publishes a 168 MHz row on the Cortex-M4 (verify 760 KCC, sign 254 KCC), the exact clock of the reference board. The study instead uses the 24 MHz row and an assumed wait state factor of 1.0 to 1.5, and the evidence table notes the 168 MHz rows were not taken because the fetch tool called their labels ambiguous. A refetch reports the rows unambiguously; the published 24 to 168 MHz ratio (760/722 = 1.05) is a direct, cited anchor for the wait state assumption that the study currently sweeps without data.
evidence: WebFetch of https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10507285 on 2026-10-20: rows 'This work, Cortex-M4, 24: 200/239/722' and 'This work, Cortex-M4, 168: 214/254/760'; S12A-331 warning 'The 168 MHz ... rows were not taken'.
suggested_fix: Double read and add the 168 MHz rows, use them to bound wait_state_factor for this code (and say it is one library), and cite them in mission/assumptions.csv.
